If finance moved tax rounding to half-up, the change is small, because the rounding isn't implemented in code yet.

**Code**
- `src/billing/tax.py`: `tax_for(amount_cents, rate)` currently just raises `NotImplementedError`, so there is no rounding mode to swap. The half-up rule would go in when the function is implemented, as `ROUND_HALF_UP` instead of `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. The invoice tax decision also adds a per-line path for `CA-QC` customers that rounds each line and then sums. It would have to use the same mode.

**Tests**
- `tests/test_tax.py`: it only imports `line_total` and has no rounding assertions. You'd add half-up cases, such as a `.5` cent tie that rounds differently under half-even.

**Probably no change**
- `scripts/backfill_tax.py`: it recomputes `tax_cents` for finalized invoices of one month. It has no rounding logic of its own, so it follows `tax_for`. Re-running it after the switch would change historical amounts. The memory notes that tax is never recomputed after finalization, so finance would need to say whether past months get backfilled.
- `src/billing/invoices.py` and `src/billing/refunds.py`: they only read `tax_cents`.
- Currency conversion uses `ROUND_FLOOR` and reporting uses 4-place quantize. Both are separate decisions and unaffected.

**Project memory**
- The EngramDB decision "Tax uses ROUND_HALF_EVEN" (March 2026, agreed with finance) says "Do not use ROUND_HALF_UP". You'd need to update or supersede it, otherwise future sessions will push back on the change. The "How invoice tax is calculated" memory may also need a mention.

I haven't changed anything.
